findings.summary: transformed_vertices accumulated a float lane with the record's now-double translation, which is C4244 under /W4 /WX -- every scene would have failed to build with MSVC, not just floating-origin ones, and clang-cl accepted it silently; it also double-rounded the non-FO bake, where the pin's allocateMat4() is a Float32Array and its GPU multiply sees the narrowed value

The mesh translation was widened at the position.set spelling only -- the sibling position.x = component write still narrowed to float and widened the rounded value back into the double field, which is the exact defect the widening exists to prevent, on a path scenes 12, 110, 116, 127 and 128 all reach

The physics pose kept its three static_cast<float> inside the widened Vec3d literal, so an integrated pose still quantized at float32 before landing in the double field; the test assertion only matched the type name and green-lit the half-change

The positional light offset was moved to light.local_matrix on the claim that it matches the pin and the writer beside it; both halves were false -- the entry writer composes its own local matrix from light.position, and the glTF punctual-light emission never writes local_matrix, so an imported light under floating origin would have been placed at the origin

CameraMatrixScalar was keyed on renderer:floating-origin while the flag it models is useHighPrecisionMatrix, which createEngine accepts on its own; a scene asking for the high-precision matrix alone got a float camera world where the pin's allocator has swapped to F64, so the feature is reached again and gates the width it names
Two doc comments the widening falsified: Vec3d claimed only the camera reaches it, and the camera record claimed camera_world_matrix always performs a float32 store

The point and spot light property tables became byte-identical objects when spot gained range; the shared colour pair and the range descriptor are each stated once now, which is the idiom commonLightProperties already established
The emitted width was re-derived from the type spelling it had just computed, so a rename of the C++ type name would silently revert the precision; the target's own property decides it
The light offset's lane lambda cast a float to double where the subtraction already promotes, and collided by name with a lambda landed in the same change that means the opposite
Both backend billboard headers computed the floating-origin offset with an identical six-line #if; one helper holds the guard, the shape draw_world already uses

A billboard's anchor is stored in a float vector and the eye is subtracted from that already-quantized lane, where the pin keeps a separate F64 anchor array for exactly this reason and computes its sort depth from the eye-relative value
findings.blockedBy: Scene 205's own source notes every anchor it uses is a multiple of 0.5, so the stored value is lossless in float32 and its 0.000 measures the plumbing rather than the width; no reached scene has an off-grid anchor at large-world scale to measure a wider store against.

findings.summary: The pin's high-precision allocator is process-global and widens every matrix it vends, including each light's local matrix, the thin-instance parent world, the navmesh merge world, the shadow-caster AABB world and the splat world; this port widened the camera's world and a node's translation and left the rest composing into float, with outer_position likewise still float
findings.blockedBy: No reached scene combines the high-precision matrix with an imported light, a thin-instance pool, a navmesh, a shadow or a splat -- assertFloatingOriginCapabilities refuses most of those pairs outright -- so a widening has nothing to be measured against.
